question: How much will Nasdaq-100 Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: rolling 10-trading-day differences between NDX and SPX price returns, 2010-2026, whose median is only ~+0.2pp (long-run NDX edge ~5pp/yr) with SD ~1.3-1.8pp depending on regime; two-week relative performance is overwhelmingly noise, so the center must sit near zero. 2026 conditions pull the center down slightly from the long-run anchor: NDX is a YTD laggard (7.8% vs SPX 9.0%, Fool/Bloomberg), the Fed hiked Sep 16 with an October hike being priced (10y at 5%), which is a duration headwind for long-duration tech, and ~$100 oil favors SPX energy weight that NDX lacks. Offsetting: NDX earnings/revenue growth still outruns SPX, semis rebounded after the Sep 14 AI-slowdown shock, the last two sessions saw NDX beat SPX (+0.61pp, +0.28pp), and Micron's Sep 30 print into a memory shortage is a plausible upside catalyst inside the window. Those cancel to roughly flat with mild left skew (NDX beta ~1.15 into risk-off; Oct 2 payrolls lands on the resolution day). Tails: a 10-day |spread| >5pp has occurred in ~1-2% of historical windows (2000-02, 2008, 2020, 2022) and the live AI-capex narrative plus an in-window semis catalyst keeps both escapes non-negligible, so 1.5% below and 1.2% above. No human market prices this spread, so no crowd blend. Evidence is regime-descriptive rather than spread-specific, so I stay close to the reference class.

calls.reconciliation: Four disputes. (1) FACTUAL, settled by arithmetic: futures carry. Run 1 had the sign backwards - futures return = cash - (r-q)dt, so NDX's lower dividend yield makes NQ decay MORE, putting NQ futures ~0.018pp BELOW cash relative to ES, as Run 3 had it. Immaterial in size but confirms Run 3's care. (2) FACTUAL, partly settled: 2026 YTD relative performance. Runs 1-2 cite a 2026-07-29 Motley Fool figure (NDX 7.8% vs SPX 9.0%) and in places the Nasdaq Composite; Run 3 cites a Sep 18 stockanalysis compare page (QQQ +17.07% vs SPY +12.01%). The current-dated quote is corroborated directionally by Invesco's primary August review (QQQ +4.22% vs SPX +2.72%) and the Sep 17-18 sessions; the July figure is stale and index-ambiguous. The two magnitudes cannot be fully bridged from the dossiers alone, so I do not treat NDX as a strong YTD leader either - I simply drop the downward shade Runs 1-2 applied to the median. (3) FACTUAL INPUT driving a JUDGMENT: dispersion. Run 2's 40% widening to 4.7pp rests on a VXN/VIX spread of 26.91 vs 17.71, but its own dossier dates that VXN to 2026-07-09 while the VIX is September - a date mismatch that inflates the spread. Run 3's same-day Sep 18 pairing (VXN-linked ~20.3, VIX 15.44-16.34) is internally consistent and yields SD 1.41-1.66pp over 10 sessions. I land at 4.0pp, above Runs 1 and 3 (3.7, 3.85) because the window carries Micron, core PCE, quarter-end flows and payrolls on resolution morning, but well below Run 2. (4) JUDGMENT, no evidence breaks it: escape mass. All three share the same ~1-2% historical base rate for |10-day spread| > 5pp, concentrated in crisis regimes this one is not; I take 1.5%/1.0% asymmetric for the left-tail mechanism, and note one concrete tail mechanism was REMOVED that Runs 1-2 did not account for - the Oct 1 shutdown deadline, eliminated by the CR signed 2026-09-02 funding through Dec 11 (Run 3 caught this). I carried Run 3's reference class forward because I agree with its construction. Also noted and discounted: two Sep 18 wire stories flagged by Runs 2 and 3 carry internally inconsistent year references, so their macro color was not used as independent confirmation; the Sep 16 hike itself is multiply corroborated. No market prices this spread on Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold, so there was no anchor to blend and nothing to reconcile there.
